'''Thomas ap Rees''' (19 October 1930 – 3 October 1996) was a [[botany|botanist]]. He was [[Professor of Botany (Cambridge University)|Professor of Botany]] in the [[Department of Plant Sciences, University of Cambridge|Department of Plant Sciences]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] between 1991 and 1996<ref name=reeswho>{{Who's Who | title=ap REES, Prof. Thomas|type=was | id = U176553 | volume = 1996 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref> when he has killed in a [[traffic collision|road accident]] whilst cycling home.<ref name="indep"/>

==Education and early life==
He was born in [[Frome]], [[Somerset]] and attended [[Llandovery College]], [[Dyfed]] and served two years [[military service]] in the [[Royal Corps of Signals]] before studying botany at [[Lincoln College, Oxford]] gaining a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in 1957 for research supervised by [[Jack Harley]].<ref name=phd>{{cite thesis |degree=DPhil |first=Thomas|last=ap Rees |title=The Effect of fungal infection upon the respoiratory metabolism of plant tissues |publisher=University of Oxford |date=1957 |url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/OXVU1:LSCOP_OX:oxfaleph020407949}}</ref>

==Research and career==
He lived in [[Sydney]], [[Australia]] for a number of years as a lecturer in botany at the [[University of Sydney]] and in 1961  he was appointed as Senior Research Officer of the [[Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation]]. He returned to Britain in 1964 on being appointed a [[lecturer]] at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name="indep">{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/obituary-professor-thomas-ap-rees-1357677.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220507/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/obituary-professor-thomas-ap-rees-1357677.html |archive-date=7 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |work=The Independent |title=Obituary: Professor Thomas ap Rees |author=David Summers, Ed Tanner and Tony Kirby|date=10 October 1996}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Ap Rees' contribution to plant [[biochemistry]] was substantial.<ref name="StittBulpin1978"/> He published over 100 research papers and more than 20 reviews during his career.<ref name="indep" /> Over 170 scientists attended a meeting held after his death in honour of him and his work. His main area of research was in the [[Metabolism#Regulation and control|regulation and control]] of plant [[metabolism]]. He argued that [[sucrose]] played a central role in plant metabolism. Much of his research was on non-[[crop]] species as he believed that there may be metabolic features present in these that could be bred into crop plants. Fellow scientists admired him for his sound approach to research.<ref>{{Cite journal| last1 = Hill | first1 = S.| title = Carbohydrate metabolism in plants| journal = Trends in Plant Science| volume = 3| issue = 10| pages = 370–371| year = 1998| doi = 10.1016/S1360-1385(98)01320-X| bibcode = 1998TPS.....3..370H}}</ref>
